description: Personal Fitness looks at fitness in body, mind and spirit, then asks you to measure where you are, design a twelve-week exercise and nutrition program, follow it, and show what changed.

safety.note: Talk with a parent or guardian, and a doctor if needed, before starting a new exercise program. Substitutions are allowed when an exercise is not safe for you.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)
Major Requirement Changes as of January 1, 2026 (scouting.org)

requirements.title: Defining fitness
requirements.summary: Physical, mental, emotional, social and spiritual fitness, why they matter, and how they relate to the Scout Oath and Law.

requirements.title: Monitoring your health
requirements.summary: Why regular physical and dental exams and daily oral care matter.

requirements.title: Fitness habits
requirements.summary: Exercise, avoiding harmful substances, vaccinations, nutrition, healthy weight, sleep and time with family and friends.

requirements.title: Measures of fitness
requirements.summary: Recording a timed mile, strength measures and a flexibility test.

requirements.title: Pre-assessment
requirements.summary: Recording your test results, finding your strongest and weakest areas, logging food and drink, and setting diet goals.

requirements.title: Planning a program
requirements.summary: A twelve-week plan with warm-up, cardio, strength, flexibility, cool-down and diet goals.

requirements.title: Completing the program
requirements.summary: Following and logging the program, retesting along the way, showing improvement and discussing results.

requirements.title: Careers or lifestyle
requirements.summary: One option: exploring fitness careers, or how a fitness activity supports a hobby or healthy lifestyle.
